//: Rate card, Home Loan Further Advance (product 40). Owner: Treasury.
//1: A THIRD REPRESENTATION: basis points OVER A REFERENCE RATE, not an absolute rate.
//2: 12 grades x 8 LTV bands x 6 term bands x 2 occupancy types = 1 152 cells.
//3: The reference rate is a SHARED param (doc 03 4.2) - `shared.reference_rate` -
//4: because it is genuinely global and must not be copied into four product bundles.
//5: The card returns a margin; products/bond_40/pricing.py turns it into a rate and
//6: records rate_basis_code=MARGIN_OVER_REFERENCE alongside both components. A record
//7: showing only 12.35% cannot be replayed when the reference rate has moved twice.

reference.name: shared.reference_rate
reference.note: Recorded, not read from here. The value in force at decision_date is resolved through core.dates and lands in the audit record beside the margin.

ltv_caps.note: The binding cap is the lowest applicable, and which one bound is recorded.

conveyancing_tariff.//: 24 amount bands x 3 components. Owner: Compliance, from the published tariff.
conveyancing_tariff.//1: Capitalised, so it feeds the circular solve: the cost depends on the advance,
conveyancing_tariff.//2: and the advance depends on the cost.
conveyancing_tariff.applies_when: advance exceeds bond_registered_amount and a NEW REGISTRATION is required

sub_term.note: THE CONSOLIDATED PORTION MUST BE CONTRACTUALLY AMORTISED OVER AT MOST 84 MONTHS, by way of a required additional payment above the bond instalment. The anti-harm rule is evaluated against that structure and not against the bond's remaining term. Without it the product's total cost is indefensible: R120 000 of card debt moved to a 240-month bond at 12% costs roughly R197 000 in interest against roughly R45 000 where it stood - a 337% increase, for a 71% instalment reduction. The instalment reduction is real, the client will want it, and it is still the wrong answer for most clients.
